messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient, a 19-year-old male with no significant past medical history, presented to the emergency room with symptoms of four hours of abdominal pain and emesis. He reported undergoing a strict regimen of dieting and exercise which resulted in significant weight loss over the past months. The family member added that the symptoms started after a heavy meal ingestion.

On physical examination, the patient presented with a scaphoid abdomen, tender abdomen and diminished high-pitched bowel sounds. The laboratory workup was within normal limits. The patient stayed overnight in the ER and was managed conservatively with NPO, intravenous crystalloid rehydration, nasogastric tube, ondansetron and omeprazole. Next day reevaluation showed persistence of abdominal pain, nausea and bilious emesis. Computed tomography study revealed gastric dilatation extended to the third portion of the duodenum, suggestive of proximal small bowel obstruction. The patient was admitted for inpatient treatment.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Management:
Initial management included gastric decompression by placing a nasojejunal feeding tube to alleviate symptoms of obstruction and later use for enteral nutritional support. The patient was provided with a normocaloric hyperproteic formula starting with 600 and progressed to 1500 kcal per day to reverse protein caloric malnutrition state. Additionally, psychiatry and psychology teams were consulted concerning major weight loss. The patient was diagnosed with depression and an eating disorder and was started on sertraline. The patient was discharged asymptomatic, with hyperproteic diet plus nutritional supplements and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

Follow-up:
The patient's follow-ups showed weight gain and no symptoms. Psychiatry and psychology teams will follow up the patient after discharge.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
This presentation fits superior mesenteric artery syndrome (Wilkie syndrome). It follows major weight loss, with gastric dilatation extending to the third part of the duodenum and a proximal obstruction on CT. The management was a nasojejunal tube with nutritional support.

In ICD-10-AM, superior mesenteric artery syndrome codes to K31.5 (obstruction of duodenum), so the three-character category is K31, "Other diseases of stomach and duodenum".

The alternatives were the eating disorder (F50) and the depression, but the condition that occasioned the admission was the duodenal obstruction. Malnutrition and the eating disorder would be additional diagnoses.

**K31**
